concept.name: Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds

relationships.description: Related to Circuit Breakers & Resilience Patterns

concept.tagline: Deduplicate concurrent in-flight lookups for identical keys so only one leader hits the origin while followers share the result.
concept.purpose: Collapse N concurrent cache-miss requests for the same key into 1 upstream origin call, protecting databases from thundering-herd overload.

spark.summary: Singleflight maintains an in-flight map of active keys so that concurrent callers for the same key await a single leader execution instead of stampeding the origin.
spark.keyTakeaway: When nodes partition or reboot past retry windows, by coalescing duplicate in-flight work behind a shared future/channel, Singleflight turns 10,000 concurrent cache misses into 1 origin query—provided you guard against shared-error amplification and context cancellation.
spark.byteSummary:
When a hot cache key expires, thousands of concurrent requests miss the cache simultaneously and slam the origin database with identical queries—a failure mode known as a cache stampede or thundering herd. Singleflight solves this at the application or proxy layer using a mutex-protected in-flight map keyed by request key.

The first caller (the leader) registers a `call` entry containing a synchronization primitive (e.g., a WaitGroup/Promise) in the map, releases the mutex, and executes the origin fetch. Subsequent callers (followers) arriving while the key is active find the existing `call` entry, release the mutex, and block on its completion signal. When the leader finishes, it stores the result/error, deletes the key from the in-flight map, and wakes all waiting followers.

In production, naive singleflight has three sharp edges: (1) a single leader failure/timeout fails all N followers simultaneously unless you support `Forget(key)` or retries; (2) if the leader's request context cancels early, it must not abort the shared fetch for remaining followers; and (3) a singleflight group only deduplicates within one process unless paired with consistent-hash routing.

learningJourney.title: Why Hot-Key Expiry Triggers Origin Collapse
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent 2,000+ concurrent cache misses on a hot key from hitting PostgreSQL simultaneously.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Why Hot-Key Expiry Triggers Origin Collapse** as the intuition layer for Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds: Prevent 2,000+ concurrent cache misses on a hot key from hitting PostgreSQL simultaneously.
explanation.core: Suppose a hot key receives 50,000 QPS and takes 40 ms to recompute from PostgreSQL. The moment its Redis TTL expires, ~2,000 concurrent requests miss Redis within that 40 ms window and all 2,000 query PostgreSQL simultaneously, exhausting connection pools and causing cascading timeouts.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, why hot-key expiry triggers origin collapse becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Cluster-wide stampede protection pairs consistent-hash coalescer routing with Singleflight, Stale-While-Revalidate, and `Forget(key)` error isolation.

learningJourney.title: Leader Election & Follower Fan-Out via In-Flight Map
learningJourney.purpose: Coordinate in-flight callers via a mutex-guarded map without holding the lock across slow network I/O.

explanation.foundation: A `SingleflightGroup` holds `mu` (a lightweight mutex) and `calls: map[key]*Call`. Callers acquire `mu` only long enough to check/insert into `calls` (nanoseconds), never across the slow network I/O.
explanation.core: If `key` exists in `calls`, the caller increments `dups`, releases `mu`, and awaits `call.done`. Otherwise, it inserts a new `Call`, releases `mu`, runs `fn()`, deletes `key` from `calls` under `mu`, and signals `call.done`.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds, watch how leader election & follower fan-out via in-flight map interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Cluster-wide stampede protection pairs consistent-hash coalescer routing with Singleflight, Stale-While-Revalidate, and `Forget(key)` error isolation.

sectionDiagram.title: Leader Election & Follower Fan-Out via In-Flight Map

cards.label: Never Lock Across I/O
cards.detail: The mutex protects only the in-memory map lookup (~50 ns), never the 40 ms database call.

cards.label: Exception Safety
cards.detail: Wrap leader execution in try/finally so the key is always removed even if fn() panics.

cards.label: Shared Future/Channel
cards.detail: Closing a Go channel or resolving a Future wakes all waiting goroutines/threads at once.

sectionDiagram.summary: Releasing the map mutex before running fn() lets thousands of keys coalesce concurrently without lock contention.
sectionDiagram.caption: Releasing the map mutex before running fn() lets thousands of keys coalesce concurrently without lock contention.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When nodes partition or reboot past retry windows, by coalescing duplicate in-flight work behind a shared future/channel, Singleflight turns 10,000 concurrent cache misses into 1 origin query—provided you guard against shared-error amplification and context cancellation.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Implementing Singleflight with Detached Contexts & Error Isolation
learningJourney.purpose: Detach the leader's context from individual caller cancellations so one client abort doesn't fail 500 followers.

explanation.foundation: Detach the leader's upstream timeout from individual caller cancellations so one impatient client cannot abort 500 waiting followers. Always wrap `fn()` in `try/finally` so the in-flight entry is cleaned up even on exception.

sectionDiagram.title: Implementing Singleflight with Detached Contexts & Error Isolation

cards.label: Caller Cancellation Bug
cards.detail: If leader inherits Caller 1's request context, Caller 1 hitting Cancel fails 500 other users.

cards.label: Detached Timeout
cards.detail: Give the leader a bounded backend context timeout independent of any single caller.

cards.label: Try/Finally Cleanup
cards.detail: A leaked entry in calls[key] would wedge every future request for that key until restart.

learningJourney.title: Mitigating Shared-Error Amplification with `Forget(key)`
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent shared-error amplification by calling Forget(key) on transient errors and bypassing negative caching.

explanation.foundation: If the leader encounters a transient 503 error, all 999 followers receive that same error. Worse, if a stale negative result is cached, traffic fails repeatedly. Using `Forget(key)` (or only coalescing healthy responses while allowing bounded jittered retry on transient errors) limits blast radius.
explanation.core: Never mutate a returned slice/object in place without cloning, because all followers share the exact same pointer/reference unless copied.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds, watch how mitigating shared-error amplification with `forget(key)` interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Cluster-wide stampede protection pairs consistent-hash coalescer routing with Singleflight, Stale-While-Revalidate, and `Forget(key)` error isolation.

cards.label: Error Amplification
cards.detail: Sharing a transient 503 across 999 followers creates a burst of user-facing errors.

cards.label: Early Forget
cards.detail: Calling Forget(key) when errors occur lets subsequent arrivals elect a fresh leader immediately.

cards.label: Bounded Follower Wait

learningJourney.title: Scaling Singleflight Across 100+ Stateless Nodes
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate N-pod amplification across 100+ stateless pods using a consistent-hash coalescer ring.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Scaling Singleflight Across 100+ Stateless Nodes** as the intuition layer for Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds: Eliminate N-pod amplification across 100+ stateless pods using a consistent-hash coalescer ring.
explanation.core: In a 100-pod Kubernetes deployment, local-only singleflight still lets 100 pods each send 1 leader request per key. Routing cache-miss traffic through a **Consistent-Hash Routing Ring** (e.g., Envoy Maglev/RingHash or an internal coalescer tier) funnels all requests for `key` to the same coalescer pod, reducing 100 origin calls down to 1.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, scaling singleflight across 100+ stateless nodes becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Cluster-wide stampede protection pairs consistent-hash coalescer routing with Singleflight, Stale-While-Revalidate, and `Forget(key)` error isolation.

learningJourney.title: Pairing Singleflight with Probabilistic Early Refresh (PER) & SWR
learningJourney.purpose: Pair Singleflight with Stale-While-Revalidate and Probabilistic Early Refresh (XFetch) to remove cold-miss waits.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Pairing Singleflight with Probabilistic Early Refresh (PER) & SWR** as the intuition layer for Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds: Pair Singleflight with Stale-While-Revalidate and Probabilistic Early Refresh (XFetch) to remove cold-miss waits.
explanation.core: Singleflight still forces callers to wait for 1 origin round-trip on expiry. Pairing Singleflight with **Stale-While-Revalidate (SWR)** or **Probabilistic Early Refresh (XFetch)** lets one background leader refresh the key before TTL=0 while all other callers receive the cached value in < 1 ms.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, pairing singleflight with probabilistic early refresh (per) & swr becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Cluster-wide stampede protection pairs consistent-hash coalescer routing with Singleflight, Stale-While-Revalidate, and `Forget(key)` error isolation.

cards.label: XFetch Early Refresh

cards.label: Zero Synchronized Spikes

learningJourney.title: When Singleflight Hurts: Non-Idempotent Writes & Personalized Auth
learningJourney.purpose: Avoid leaking cross-tenant data or coalescing non-idempotent writes by keying strictly on full auth scope.

explanation.foundation: Think of **When Singleflight Hurts: Non-Idempotent Writes & Personalized Auth** as the intuition layer for Singleflight Request Coalescing: Eliminating Thundering Herds: Avoid leaking cross-tenant data or coalescing non-idempotent writes by keying strictly on full auth scope.
explanation.core: Never coalesce requests whose key omits tenant ID, auth scope, or user permissions—doing so leaks one user's private payload to 999 followers. Also never coalesce non-idempotent mutations (`POST /charge`) unless keyed by an explicit client idempotency token.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, when singleflight hurts: non-idempotent writes & personalized auth becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Cluster-wide stampede protection pairs consistent-hash coalescer routing with Singleflight, Stale-While-Revalidate, and `Forget(key)` error isolation.

sectionDiagram.title: When Singleflight Hurts: Non-Idempotent Writes & Personalized Auth

cards.label: Cross-Tenant Leak
cards.detail: If follower B shares key 'dashboard' with leader A without tenant_id, B receives A's private data.

cards.label: Read-Only Rule
cards.detail: Never coalesce state-mutating POST/PATCH requests unless keyed by an explicit Idempotency-Key.

cards.label: Vary Headers
cards.detail: Include locale, currency, and permission tier in the singleflight key.

sectionDiagram.summary: Including tenant/auth scope in every key and restricting singleflight to idempotent reads prevents data leaks.
sectionDiagram.caption: Including tenant/auth scope in every key and restricting singleflight to idempotent reads prevents data leaks.

beginner.summary: Singleflight makes sure that if 1,000 users ask for the same uncached item at once, only 1 request goes to the database and everyone shares the answer.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When nodes partition or reboot past retry windows, by coalescing duplicate in-flight work behind a shared future/channel, Singleflight turns 10,000 concurrent cache misses into 1 origin query—provided you guard against shared-error amplification and context cancellation.
beginner.byteSummary:
When a popular cache item expires, thousands of users can hit the database at the exact same millisecond. Singleflight puts a small checklist in memory: the first request goes to the database while the other 999 wait quietly for that one answer.

Once the answer returns, everyone gets a copy and the database stays safe.

intermediate.summary: Singleflight uses a mutex-guarded in-flight map and shared Event/Promise to collapse duplicate concurrent misses into one origin call.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When nodes partition or reboot past retry windows, by coalescing duplicate in-flight work behind a shared future/channel, Singleflight turns 10,000 concurrent cache misses into 1 origin query—provided you guard against shared-error amplification and context cancellation.
intermediate.byteSummary:
A `SingleflightGroup` coordinates concurrent callers by key. The leader inserts a `Call` object, runs the origin fetch, removes the key in a `finally` block, and wakes all followers.

Production implementations bound follower wait times, isolate leader cancellations, and include tenant/auth dimensions in the key.

advanced.summary: Cluster-wide stampede protection pairs consistent-hash coalescer routing with Singleflight, Stale-While-Revalidate, and `Forget(key)` error isolation.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When nodes partition or reboot past retry windows, by coalescing duplicate in-flight work behind a shared future/channel, Singleflight turns 10,000 concurrent cache misses into 1 origin query—provided you guard against shared-error amplification and context cancellation.
advanced.byteSummary:
At fleet scale, local singleflight leaves an N-pod amplification factor. Placing a consistent-hash coalescing ring in front of the origin collapses cluster-wide misses to 1.

Pairing Singleflight with Stale-While-Revalidate and Probabilistic Early Refresh eliminates miss-latency spikes entirely while `Forget(key)` limits error blast radius.

prerequisites.title: Distributed & Application Caching
prerequisites.summary: Caching keeps a reusable copy of data so an application can avoid repeating a database query, calculation, or network call. It can make responses faster and reduce database load. The trade-off: the copy may be out of date.

prerequisites.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
prerequisites.summary: Consistent hashing assigns data keys to servers in a way that limits how many keys move when servers are added or removed. This helps avoid widespread cache misses and sudden load on databases.

prerequisites.title: Circuit Breaker Pattern
prerequisites.summary: A stateful proxy that monitors downstream failures and slow calls over a sliding window, tripping open to fail fast in microseconds instead of letting 2,000ms+ timeouts exhaust caller thread pools.
